title: Denmark’s GomSpace Secures €8M Contract for Blue Origin Moon Mission
html:
Danish satellite manufacturer GomSpace has secured an €8 million contract to continue developing two spacecraft for Blue Origin’s lunar resource prospecting mission.

In its 19 November announcement confirming the start of phase two of the project’s development, GomSpace did not identify Blue Origin as the customer, referring to it only as a “leading North American space company.” The company did, however, outline the mission, saying it would “deploy two satellites into orbit around the Moon to conduct resource prospecting in support of future lunar exploration.”

During the company’s Q1 earnings call in May, GomSpace CEO Carsten Drachmann explained that it was working on a mission for Blue Origin that would involve “two satellites orbiting around the moon.” Later, during its Q3 2026 investor presentation earlier this month, Drachmann said the mission for Blue Origin was “about mapping out the moon” and “looking for minerals” to mine.

GomSpace announced in January that it had received an initial €2.9 million contract for the mission, which covered the preliminary design of the two spacecraft. The newly announced €8 million agreement brings the project’s total value to €10.9 million.

Under the second phase, GomSpace will continue developing the two spacecraft towards operational capability. The company explained that the mission’s next major milestones include a critical design review and the integration of scientific payloads in the United States. Delivery of the spacecraft is expected in late 2027.

The two spacecraft are being developed for Oasis-1, the first mission under Blue Origin’s broader Project Oasis initiative.

Unveiled in September 2025, the initiative aims to identify, assess, and eventually utilise resources found on the Moon. The project is being developed in partnership with Luxembourg. The collaboration was announced in June 2025, with Blue Origin signing a cooperation agreement with Luxembourg’s Ministry of the Economy and announcing plans to establish a European office in the country.

Oasis-1 will focus on mapping lunar resources, including water ice, helium-3, rare earth elements and precious metals. The mission is intended to identify potential extraction sites and assess the availability of materials that could eventually support a sustained human presence on the Moon.
summary: Denmark’s GomSpace has secured an €8 million contract to develop two satellites for Blue Origin’s lunar resource prospecting mission.
